tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Read memory. With only a query (op omitted, or op=semantic): rows ranked by relevance — who the user is, their preferences and decisions, not codebase facts. op=get fetches one row by id; op=list browses by filters without ranking (audits, a day's worklist). Pass the fewest filters that answer the question; scope_root is the host's to fill.

op.description: omit op for semantic · semantic: query, tier?, scope_root?, limit? · list: tier?, types?, scope_root?, indexed?, past_ttl?, day?, unjudged?, sort?, limit?, offset? · get: id

query.description: Natural-language description of what to find.

tier.description: Restrict to one tier. Omit to span all.

scope_root.description: op=semantic: HOST-FILLED — leave it out; the host stamps the session root, which weighs each row by how near its stored scope is to the root (a skill's dir sees only its own rows). · op=list: A session root: rows whose stored scope is under it or at its parents, and rows about the person (no scope). A skill's dir sees only its own rows.

indexed.description: Only indexed rows (true) or only the rest (false).

past_ttl.description: Return only rows past the configured episodic TTL. Implies tier=episodic.

day.description: One local calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD — the remember stage lists a single day's worklist with this.

unjudged.description: With day: only the rows no remember pass has judged yet — a re-opened day's new rows, not the whole day.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description: Save one durable row — identity, a preference, a decision with its why — not project internals or secrets. Default tier episodic, from derived; the user's own words are from=user. scope is the directory the row is about (one of the session's scope candidates), global:true when it is about the person. A standing rule gets indexed:true and a one-line summary. host, source_session, cwd and root are the host's to fill. Merge your own rows atomically with replace_ids, never add then delete; replacing a from=user row needs the user's answer and user_directed:true. occurred_at (RFC 3339) dates an imported or promoted row.

content.description: The fact text the model will see when this row is recalled.

from.description: Whose words: user = the user stated it (a preference, a decision, a fact about them); agent = you did or observed it; derived (default) = your inference.

tier.description: Destination tier: episodic = per-turn staging (the default when omitted, no search-first); semantic = curated durable facts (search-first); core = tiny always-injected universals (search-first). Doctrine in the server instructions.

scope.description: The directory this row is about, when it is not where you stand: one of the session's "Memory scopes here" candidates (e.g. skills/lingjing, ~/workspace). Omit for the session's own directory. Stored as the row's `scope` (absolute path; none = about the person).

summary.description: One line, ≤ 80 chars: what this row is for — what the index shows in its place. Matters on indexed rows; without one the index shows the row's opening.

indexed.description: true = put the row in its scope's index: its summary loads at every session start in that directory or below. For standing rules the user states ("always…", "from now on…").

host.description: HOST-FILLED — leave it out; the host stamps the committing runtime.

source_session.description: HOST-FILLED — leave it out; the host stamps this session. Only a promote pass carrying an original row's session forward passes it.

cwd.description: HOST-FILLED, request only — leave it out; the host stamps the session's working directory: the stored scope when you name none, and the base a named one is checked against. Never stored under this name.

root.description: HOST-FILLED — leave it out; the host stamps the session root that `scope` resolves against.

global.description: true = the row is about the person, not a directory: stored with no scope, recalled everywhere.

replace_ids.description: Row ids this row replaces — inserted and deleted atomically. For merges and resolved conflicts; never separate add + delete calls.

user_directed.description: Assert the user directed this change (a settled command/declaration, or they just answered your ask). Required when replace_ids targets from=user rows — memory BLOCKS such writes otherwise. Hedged reflections don't qualify; see the server instructions.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 time the row is about — for an imported or promoted row; dates its day and TTL, never its rank.

tools.name: memory_update
tools.description: Edit one row in place by id (content, type, tier, scope or global, summary, indexed); a tier change keeps the id. Rewriting a from=user row's content needs the user's answer and user_directed:true. To merge several rows use memory_add with replace_ids.

tier.description: Moving tier relocates the row across tables, id preserved.

scope.description: Move the row: its stored scope, the absolute directory it is about (~/… allowed).

summary.description: New one-line summary (≤ 80 chars) — what the index shows for an indexed row.

indexed.description: Put the row in (true) or take it out of (false) its scope's index.

global.description: true = clear the row's stored scope so it applies everywhere.

user_directed.description: Required when rewriting content on a from=user row — see memory_add.user_directed.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Hard-delete one row by id: an explicit forget, an exact duplicate, a secret saved by mistake. Never part of a merge — memory_add with replace_ids does that in one call.

tools.name: memory_upkeep
tools.description: Memory upkeep, one op per step of the scan, dream and solve runbooks (the Linggen plugin's skill references). Ops here: session_start, harvest_day, days, remember_day, dream_lease, role, sweep, issues, issue_add, issue_resolve, chains, dream_status, dream_run. session_start is the host's call at session start. Each op keeps its own checks: past local days only, the dream lease, the primary. issues lists the review queue; you solve each item from evidence and close it with issue_resolve. dream_status: undreamed days, first_unscanned, open_issues, in_flight, the last run and its failures; show last_run_error, and last_run_cannot_run says why a run could not go on (reason, model, resets_at, line). Offer the dream with your own model (the dream runbook) when days await it. dream_run runs the dream on this machine's Linggen model and returns at once; read dream_status afterwards.

op.description: session_start: cwd?, root? · harvest_day: date · days: undreamed_only?, from?, to? · remember_day: date, judged?, promoted?, holder? · dream_lease: day, holder, action? · role: no fields · sweep: dry_run? · issues: status?, limit? · issue_add: kind, row_ids?, note · issue_resolve: id, outcome, note? · chains: kind?, limit?, offset?, derived_only? · dream_status: no fields · dream_run: day?

root.description: HOST-FILLED — the session's root (git root, or where it started).

undreamed_only.description: Only days awaiting a dream pass (the worklist).

promoted.description: Rows promoted to semantic in this pass.

holder.description: op=remember_day: The dream lease holder, when one was taken. · op=dream_lease: Who is dreaming, e.g. claude-code@<host>.

day.description: op=dream_lease: Local calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. · op=dream_run: Optional target day, YYYY-MM-DD — one-day scoped run (the calendar shape)

dry_run.description: Report what would be evicted without deleting.

limit.description: op=issues: Max items (default 50). · op=chains: Clusters per page (default 10).

kind.description: op=issue_add: What you saw: `chain` = uncertain merge candidate; `stale-status` = a status claim likely overtaken by the world (verify against git/files at solve time); `contradiction` = conflicting rows needing the user's pick; `subject` = digest cluster of doubtful subject coherence (list ALL member ids). Scope, index and summary fixes are not queued — the dream applies them itself. · op=chains: cited (default) = id-citation chains; marker = provisional-state candidates; subject = same-subject clusters for digests.

row_ids.description: The memory row ids this item is about.

note.description: op=issue_add: What you saw and what a solver should check — the item's whole context, since the solver starts from this line alone. Write it in plain words; it may become the user's question. · op=issue_resolve: One-line record of what was done.

offset.description: Pagination offset over the cluster list.

derived_only.description: Only clusters mergeable unattended (every row from=derived, tier=semantic). Unattended condense passes MUST set true.

tools.name: agent_run
tools.description: Delegate to a local Linggen agent; only its final reply returns, its steps show in the web UI. For code changes create a git worktree and pass its absolute path as write_dir with your permission_mode (plan = read-only, default/acceptEdits = edit, auto/bypassPermissions = admin there; other paths stay read-only). grants adds read/write folders, screened per folder. Continue with session_id, omitting write_dir, permission_mode and model. model_fallback defaults false: a failing model ends the run naming the model and reason. Watch the returned ws://…/api/agent/wait URL: permission_request (answer with agent_permit) and finished (reply, followup, error, model, and cannot_run when the run could not go on: reason, model, resets_at, line, work_kept).

prompt.description: Self-contained brief: files, cause, tests to run, and ask for a short reply

session_id.description: Continue an existing session with its context; omit write_dir, permission_mode and model

model.description: Model for a new session; agent_status op=models lists which are ready

agent.description: Agent to run (default: ling). Unknown names return the available list.

model_fallback.description: Default false: if the model fails the run ends naming the model and the reason, rather than switching to another model; true allows the automatic switch.

host.description: Calling host, e.g. claude-code, codex or cursor (default claude-code)

permission_mode.description: Your current permission mode; plan is read-only, default/acceptEdits grant edit, auto/bypassPermissions grant admin in write_dir only. New sessions only.

work.description: New sessions: code adds coding guidance and lets the run run programs where it may edit without asking (outward commands still ask you); defaults to code with write_dir, otherwise none; ignored on continuation.

write_dir.description: For code changes, create a git worktree first and pass its existing absolute path. The grant follows permission_mode; other paths stay read-only, and an action beyond that waits for your agent_permit. Omit for read-only; new sessions only (a continued session keeps its grant).

grants.description: New sessions only: folders the run may use without asking. read: folders to read. write: more folders at write_dir's level. Folders your level does not allow are refused; the run still starts, and the reply and agent_status (grants) list what was granted and refused, with reasons. Programs need no grant: a run with write_dir runs them where it may edit.

tools.name: agent_status
tools.description: op=session: one session's running work, pending permission requests, status, error, the model that answered, reply, followup, denied actions, grants and cannot_run (why it stopped: a usage limit carries resets_at) — once when a watch ends without finished; never poll. It also carries usage, what the session's model calls used and cost: per-model tokens, cost_usd only for a model with a known price, the total, and unpriced (models whose tokens the total leaves out). op=models: every model and whether it can be used now (ready, or why not and what to do); pick a ready one for agent_run's model.

tools.name: agent_permit
tools.description: Answer a session's permission request (a permission_request event, or agent_status pending). A cut Bash summary carries the whole command: read it first. allow_once runs that action; allow_session grants its path (scope=path) or folder (scope=dir) for the session; an outward request takes allow_once or deny only; deny refuses. Unanswered requests are denied after 10 minutes.

scope.description: allow_session only: the exact target, or its folder (default dir when grantable)

tools.name: agent_end
tools.description: op=stop cancels a session's running turn and subagents. op=close stops it and, with remove_worktree=true after you reviewed and merged, removes its linked worktree — only a clean one whose HEAD is on a remote branch.

remove_worktree.description: Remove the clean, remote-contained linked worktree after work stops (default false)

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Load a page in the one visible Chrome tab Linggen controls: op=navigate (an absolute URL, or back/forward) or op=tab_open (an absolute URL, creating the tab if needed). Chrome may ask the user to allow this site; they approve or decline there.

url.description: op=navigate: Absolute URL to load, or "back" / "forward" · op=tab_open: Absolute URL to open in the controlled tab, creating it if needed

tools.name: browser_read
tools.description: Read the controlled tab: op=page (accessibility tree with refs like n42 for browser_act; refs go stale after the page changes, so read again), op=screenshot (an image, for what the tree cannot show), op=console (recent messages), op=tabs (its state).

op.description: page: filter? · screenshot: region? · tabs: no fields · console: limit?

region.description: Optional viewport region to capture; omit for the full viewport

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Act in the controlled tab: click (ref or coordinate), type, key, scroll, wait (load, selector, or ms), tab_switch, tab_close. Read the page again after it changes. Chrome may ask the user to allow this site; they approve or decline there.

op.description: click: ref?, coordinate?, button?, double? · type: text, ref?, clear? · key: keys, repeat? · scroll: direction, amount?, ref? · wait: for, value? · tab_switch: no fields · tab_close: no fields

ref.description: op=click: Node ref from browser_read op=page, e.g. "n42" · op=type: Field ref from browser_read op=page; omit to use current focus · op=scroll: Scroll at this node instead of page center

coordinate.description: Viewport [x, y] — only when no ref exists for the target

tools.name: app
tools.description: Use what the person's apps do on this Mac, such as playing music: op=list shows each app with what it is for and its actions; with app, that app's actions with their arguments. op=call runs one (app, action, args) and returns its result. A destructive action is refused: the person does it in the app. A private app answers only once the owner opens it to outside agents in Linggen's Settings.

op.description: list: app? · call: app, action, args?

app.description: op=list: An app's name; omit to list every app that offers an action · op=call: The app's name

action.description: The action to run, as op=list names it

args.description: The action's arguments, as op=list shows them

tools.name: memory_agents
tools.description: What other agents (Claude Code, Codex) remember, read from their own files. Linggen only reads: it never edits, moves or copies them, and each agent keeps its memory its own way. op=index: their index lines for a project (cwd), never the calling host's own (host); op=read: one note by path, only inside those memories; op=search: words across them, any language. For this Mac's owner at this Mac.

op.description: mode: no fields · index: cwd?, host? · read: path · search: words, limit?

cwd.description: The project folder; the nearest project's lines come first

host.description: The calling host, e.g. claude-code or codex: its own memory is left out

path.description: A note's absolute path (or ~/…), as the index names its folder and file

words.description: Words to find (any language, any case); a line with more of them ranks higher

limit.description: Most lines to return (default 10, at most 30)

tools.name: memory_notes
tools.description: Linggen's own notes about the person and the work. op=index lists the notes for a project; op=read opens one note (id) or a topic file (path); op=search finds notes by words, any language, and what other agents remember; op=write adds a note (scope, topic, summary, kind, body) or changes one by id (action update, void, no_raise, yearly). Write only a fact the person asked to remember, a decision or rule with its why, or a gotcha — never what was done or where work stands. A note in the person's own voice changes only after you show it and they agree (user_directed true). Notes about the body, mind and people close to the person, life moments, and the chronicle (what the person did, month by month) are Yinyue's alone.

op.description: index: cwd?, host? · read: id?, path? · search: words?, limit? · write: action?, scope?, topic?, summary?, kind?, voice?, body?, id?, reason?, on?, user_directed?, base?, day?, host?

cwd.description: The project folder; its notes come first

host.description: The calling host, e.g. claude-code or codex: recorded as the writer

id.description: A note's id, from the index

path.description: A topic file inside the store, e.g. person/diet.md

words.description: Words to find (any language, any case); a note with more of them ranks higher

action.description: Default add (update when an id is given)

scope.description: add: person | area:<body|mind|people|music|money|play|home> | project:<absolute path> | moments | chronicle

topic.description: add: the topic file's name; in the chronicle a month (2026-11) or a year (2026)

voice.description: add: user for the person's own words

body.description: What, and for a rule, decision or gotcha the why

reason.description: void: why the note is wrong

on.description: no_raise: true (default) = never bring it up unasked

user_directed.description: true only after the person agreed to change a note in their own voice

base.description: The version of the topic file you read

day.description: yearly: the day the note repeats every year, MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD (a birthday, an anniversary); empty clears it
